title: The bubble: arbitration with the targets runtime, clipping, wording, announcements
owns: packages/bubble/**, app/main/agent/presenter.ts (not friendlyError), the bubble-writing parts of app/main/targets/runtime.ts, app/renderer/overlay/target-copy.ts and the bubble owner

findings.title: offer_connect's Connect button is overwritten within milliseconds by the conversation's own bubble
findings.scenario: The user says "open the logs on build-01" while build-01 isn't connected. The model calls offer_connect, and the runtime writes "Connect to build-01? [Connect] [Not now]" straight to main's setState, bypassing the BubbleOwner. When tool.execution_complete arrives a few ms later, Presenter.apply (presenter.ts:749-752) re-pushes the conversation's own bubble and wipes the offer. The tool result has told the model "Ember showed the user a Connect button... Tell them to click it", so Ember then says "Click Connect" with no button on screen. The headline 'name a computer, get a Connect button' flow is effectively dead for the user.
findings.evidence: Scratch vitest with the real Presenter and the real buildTargets rig, both writing through guardWhileAsking. Screen log: 'Thinking…' -> 'Connect to build-01? | You asked for build-01 [Connect/Not now]' -> 'Thinking…' again, then after the tool-complete line 'Ember | I've shown a Connect button. []'. The final screen has no actions. Code: runtime.ts:547-552 (bubble() calls deps.showState directly), runtime.ts:1383-1388 (offerConnect), main.ts:1475 (showState: setState, no owner), presenter.ts:395-412 (apply consults only the owner, which doesn't know the runtime wrote).
findings.fix: Make runtime bubbles owners in the BubbleOwner. Expose an AgentHost method such as agent.showNotice(key, bubble, {holdUntil}) that does a 'take' claim and sets owner.holder to a runtime token until the bubble is answered, expires or is hidden. Presenters then queue behind it as they do behind a question. Alternatively route offer_connect through the Confirmer, which already gives hold, arming, timeout and keys. At minimum, hold the owner while an actionable runtime bubble is up.

findings.title: Runtime info-bubble timers blank whatever replaced them; stale presenter hide timers blank runtime bubbles
findings.scenario: After connecting, Ember shows "Ember is on build-01 / Ask away: I'll work there" for 7 s (INFO_MS). The user takes that invitation and asks at 3 s. The answer streams and finishes at about 5 s. At 7 s the runtime's timer calls hideBubble, which unconditionally writes IDLE_BUBBLE, and the answer disappears after about 2 s instead of its 7+ s reading time, along with its 'Read all' button. It works the other way too: an earlier answer's presenter hide timer still believes it owns the screen and blanks a runtime bubble shown meanwhile, such as 'Lost build-01 [Reconnect] [Stop trying]' or an offer.
findings.evidence: Scratch vitest. (1) connect, then userPrompt, then answer, then idle, then fire the runtime timers: the answer thought is "There are 12 files in /var/log…" before and visible=false thought="" after. (2) answer on screen with hide armed for 7100 ms, then link 'lost' bubble shown, then the answer's hide timer fires: screen visible=false, title "". Code: runtime.ts:551 checks only shown?.seq (its own sequence) and runtime.ts:553-557 writes IDLE_BUBBLE; compare main.ts:429-431 hideIfStill, which checks lastState.bubble === bubble. presenter.ts:510-518 hide() pushes IDLE whenever owner.current === this, which the runtime's write never changes.
findings.fix: In hideBubble, only clear if the bubble on screen is still the one it wrote (keep the object and compare with lastState, as hideIfStill does). Make Presenter.hide do the same check before pushing IDLE. The proper fix is the owner routing described in the previous finding.

findings.title: "Lost build-01 [Reconnect]" is replaced by the stopped task's bare "Stopped.", and Ember silently works on this computer
findings.scenario: A task is running on build-01 and the network drops. The runtime calls stopTasks, then shows 'Lost build-01 — The connection dropped… [Reconnect] [Stop trying]', and resets the active target to this computer (line 656). A moment later the aborted worker finishes as 'cancelled', and host.ts:875-876 shows presenter.outcome({title: task, text: 'Stopped.', mood: 'idle'}). That replaces the Lost bubble, so the user sees 'Check disk on build-01 — Stopped.' for about 6 s and then nothing. The Reconnect button is gone, the wording blames no one, and the handle badge has already gone (active target is local). The next request without a place word runs on this PC, and nothing said so.
findings.evidence: Scratch vitest log: 'Lost build-01 [Reconnect/Stop trying]' then 'Check disk []', final on screen 'Check disk []'. Worker result for an abort is stoppedSummary() = 'Stopped.' (worker.ts:1246, 1352), and TaskManager maps abort to 'cancelled' (tasks.ts:256). runtime.ts:652-660 (lost branch) and :656 (setActive(LOCAL_TARGET)); host.ts:870-876 only silences kill-switch stops.
findings.fix: Hold the Lost bubble in the owner (see the first finding). Give tasks cut off by a lost link a reason ('build-01 dropped, so I stopped this') instead of 'Stopped.'. Add 'Until it's back I'll work on this computer' to the Lost text. Keep the bubble until the user acts or SA's reconnect succeeds.

findings.title: Short answers with line breaks are clipped to six lines with no "Read all"; the question at the end is cut off
findings.scenario:
Ember answers 'You have three options:

1. Move the files…

2. Delete the duplicates

3. Leave everything as it is

Which would you like?' (134 characters). The bubble shows only the header and two options. The fade at the bottom is invisible because the sixth line is blank. Option 3 and the question are hidden, no 'Read all' is offered, and the bubble hides after about 9 s. The user decides on half an answer. Lists and paragraph breaks are the model's normal style, so this is common.
findings.evidence: Chromium render of the built overlay: this answer measures 9 lines needed and 6 available, data-overflow=true, 0 buttons (screenshot s-options.png in the scratch folder). A 93-character 7-item list also overflows with no button. Cause: presenter.ts:768-769 offers 'Read all' only when full.length > LONG_ANSWER (260 characters), while the CSS clamp (bubble.ts:240-244) is 6 lines and pre-line keeps every newline.
findings.fix: Decide by lines, not characters: estimate rendered lines as the sum of max(1, ceil(line.length/36)) over the answer's lines and offer 'Read all' when that exceeds 6. Better, let the bubble measure overflow after layout (it already computes `over`) and have the overlay add the ui:more action when a finished answer overflows.

findings.title: "On <computer>" exists only as a visual badge: missing from screen-reader announcements, spoken questions, notifications, the no-compositor card and fill_cells questions
findings.platforms: all (SSH and WSL targets); the card on Linux xrdp/VNC (no compositor)
findings.scenario: A task on build-01 asks "May I? Click Save in gedit?". Sighted users on the compositor path see a 'on build-01' capsule. A screen-reader user hears 'Ember needs you: May I? Click “Save” in gedit?' with no computer named. With speech on, main speaks 'Ember asks: Click Save in gedit? Press Ctrl+Alt+Y…'. When the user is idle, the notification says 'Ember needs your OK: Click “Save” in gedit?'. In a no-compositor session (xrdp/VNC) the corner card never renders BubbleState.where or TaskCard.where, and its header shows the picker's target instead. With build-01 picked and a task bound to this computer, the card says 'build-01' beside a question about this PC. The fill_cells question (worker.ts:2513) carries no `where` at all. Approving a step without knowing which computer it is on defeats the 'one computer per task, questions say where' guarantee.
findings.evidence: announcement() (bubble.ts:50-61) takes only title and thought; the badge is DOM-only in overlay/main.ts:164-174. Ran announcement(): connected -> 'Ember says: Ask away…' (host dropped); question -> no place. main.ts:691 and :693 use q.question.prompt with no where; worker.ts:3366 even comments 'a badge in the bubble, and in the spoken question' but no code speaks it; handle/main.ts renders only s.target (Chromium render s-fallback.png: the card text contains no where). worker.ts:2513 passes no where.
findings.fix: Add `where` to BubbleView and prepend it in announcement() ('Ember needs you, on build-01: …'). Pass q.question.where into the spoken text and notification in main.ts questionChanged. Render b.where and task.where in the fallback card, preferring them over the picker badge. Add where to the fill_cells question.

findings.title: Unsolicited offers never expire, park Ember where it stands, and take clicks immediately
findings.scenario: The user runs `ssh build-01` in a terminal. Ember pops 'You're connected to build-01 — Bring Ember there too? [Bring Ember] [Not now] [Don't offer again]' beside the cursor. If they ignore it, the bubble has no timer, and any bubble with actions makes overlay.ts setState park the follower, so Ember stops following the cursor and sits frozen with a pulsing 'Needs you' chip until a button is pressed or Ember happens to speak. A user who clicks in the terminal near the cursor can hit 'Bring Ember' or the permanent 'Don't offer again' at once, because (unlike a question) these buttons have no arming delay. The WSL offer and offer_connect's Connect behave the same.
findings.evidence: showSeenOffer (runtime.ts:963-976), offerWsl (:1049-1054) and offerConnect (:1383-1388) call bubble() with no hideMs. overlay.ts:127-152: waiting(s) is true when bubble.actions.length > 0, which calls follower.park(here()); follower.step then returns parked ?? target (follow.ts:79-88). The 500 ms arm exists only in the Confirmer (confirm.ts:98) and the renderer arms only task: ids (arm.ts). The greeting, by contrast, hides after 7 or 15 s (main.ts:454).
findings.fix: Give offers a 20-30 s expiry that counts as 'Not now' (without writing the permanent dismissal). Don't park the follower for unsolicited offers. Ignore presses in the first 500 ms as the Confirmer does.

findings.title: "Needs you" mood is used for information-only notices; other state words are borrowed too
findings.scenario: 'Stopped on build-01 — Someone at build-01 pressed Stop.', 'Back on this computer', and the screen-locked notice need nothing from the user, yet they render a purple pulsing 'Needs you' chip. A screen reader announces 'Ember needs you: Stopped on build-01…'. 'Ember is on build-01' shows a green 'Done' chip. 'Connecting to build-01…' shows a 'Thinking' chip with the thinking glow. A signed-out request gets the red 'Problem' notice while the same state's greeting is purple 'Needs you'. These runtime bubbles also never set Ember's emotion, so a 'Problem' bubble sits on a neutral face. docs/DESIGN.md defines Needs you as 'asking before a risky step'.
findings.evidence: Rendered in Chromium (s-stoppedRemote.png, s-connecting.png, s-connected.png). Announcement output: 'Ember needs you: Stopped on build-01. Someone at build-01 pressed Stop.' runtime.ts:617, 623, 668 use mood "attention" with no actions; BUBBLE_LABEL (bubble.ts:21-30) has no connecting or info state; announcement() maps attention to 'needs you' (bubble.ts:56). host.ts:1356 (notice, mood error) vs main.ts:449 (greeting, attention).
findings.fix: Use mood idle (chip hidden) for pure notices. Add a 'connecting' label and mood (or a chip override) for connection progress. Use 'attention' only when a button needs a decision. Pass an emotion with runtime error and notice bubbles.

findings.title: Bubble titles truncate with an ellipsis exactly where they carry the decision
findings.scenario: With the state chip (and a 'where' badge) sharing the header row, the one-line title is ellipsized. The command announcement 'Pushing feature-x to origin, as you asked' (the thing the user may want to Stop in 4 s) shows as 'Pushing feature-x to origin, as you …'. 'You're connected to build-01 from Ubuntu-22.04' loses the distro. With a badge, a task title like 'Tidy the desktop logs and rotate them' shows as 'Tidy …' when the host is a FQDN, and the badge itself reads 'on ip-10-0-12-34.eu-west-1.…', hiding the end of the name.
findings.evidence: Measured in Chromium (scrollWidth > clientWidth on .eb-title). Without a badge: 'Pushing feature-x…' need=273 avail=253; 'You're connected to build-01 from Ubuntu-22.04' need=325 avail=253. With 'on build-01': 'Copilot didn't accept the sign-in', 'Turn on commands on this computer?', 'Can't connect to build-01' and 19 more cut at avail 151-175. CSS at bubble.ts:238 (.eb-title nowrap/ellipsis) and overlay/styles.css (.where max-width 160px).
findings.fix: Let the title wrap to two lines in attention and announcement moods, or move the statement into the thought. Shorten the badge from the middle (keep the host's start and end) and cap it lower.

findings.title: Error bubbles clip at six lines with no scroll or expand; ssh messages show literal backticks
findings.scenario: 'Can't connect to build-01' with the host-key-changed message (255 characters) is cut at the last line and loses 'then connect again.'. A long hostname pushes the `ssh-keygen -R <host>` fix off the bottom. The sign-in-refused message plus a proxy note (265 characters) is also cut. Only attention bubbles scroll (up to 10 lines). The message also shows its backticks verbatim ('`ssh-keygen -R build-01`'), since runtime bubbles bypass plainMarkdown. fail() hides it after 14 s.
findings.evidence: Chromium: error mood, keyChanged needs 7 lines and has 6 (overflow=true); signinProxy 7 vs 6; the same texts fit in attention mood (s-keychanged.png). CSS: bubble.ts:240-244 (6-line clamp) vs :262-265 (attention scrolls). Texts from remote/ssh-errors.ts:45-48 (keyChanged + keyChangedFix) and host.ts:345.
findings.fix: Treat error like attention (scroll up to 10 lines), or raise the error clamp to 8. Strip backticks (or render them as code) in runtime-sourced text. Keep the actionable sentence first.

findings.title: Error bubbles tell the user to open settings but only some have the button
findings.scenario: A session.error for a refused sign-in reads 'Copilot didn't accept the sign-in. Open settings to sign in again.' or 'Pick another one in settings (Ctrl+Alt+E)', but that bubble has actions: [] (line 780), so there is nothing to click. A failed task's outcome has none either. fail() and the not-ready notice always add 'Open settings', even for a transient 'Copilot stopped unexpectedly. I'm reconnecting' or a pure network outage where settings can't help, and the bubble then says 'Press Check again', a settings-window button.
findings.evidence: presenter.ts:773-785 (session.error: actions: []) vs :521-533 (fail: Open settings always) and host.ts:1356 (notice: Open settings always). friendlyError texts at presenter.ts:46 and :48. explainStartError 'Press Check again' (host.ts:341) and host.ts:1183 surface in the bubble.
findings.fix: Derive the button from the failure class: add 'Open settings' to session.error when friendlyError points to settings (sign-in, model, no access), and drop it for network and transient errors. Phrase bubble text without references to settings-window buttons.

findings.title: Queued tasks show the purple "?" and are read as "Needs you:"
findings.scenario: With two tasks running, a third queues. Its card detail says 'Waiting to start', but TaskManager publishes status 'waiting', so the card shows the 'waits for you' symbol in purple and screen readers hear 'Needs you: <task> Waiting to start'. The user is told something is needed from them when nothing is.
findings.evidence: tasks.ts:292 maps queued to 'waiting'; overlay/main.ts:236 and handle/main.ts STATE_WORD.waiting = 'Needs you: '; shared/ember.css:170 draws the waiting symbol in --purple.
findings.fix: Add a distinct 'queued' card status (neutral symbol, 'Queued: '), or map queued to running with the detail 'Waiting for a free slot'. Keep 'waiting' for tasks that are asking.

findings.title: Connection progress rewrites the bubble on every download chunk
findings.scenario: First connection to a host downloads Node (about 30 MB). The progress callback fires per network chunk, each firing calls bubble() and a full-state IPC to the overlay and the handle, although the text ('12 of 29 MB') changes only about 30 times. On a fast link that is hundreds to thousands of state pushes per second on the main thread and two renderers.
findings.evidence: Scratch vitest: 30 MB in 16 KB chunks produced 1832 showState calls with a bubble but only 31 distinct texts. Callback per chunk at remote/runtime-download.ts:176; runtime.ts:1108-1109 (bubble per progress event) and remote/connections.ts:396.
findings.fix: Skip the write when progressWords() equals the last words, or throttle to about 4 per second.

findings.title: State chip and title repeat each other ('Thinking | Thinking…', 'Listening | Listening…', 'Showing you | Showing you')
findings.scenario: While thinking the header reads 'Thinking  Thinking…'. When listening: 'Listening  Listening…'. For a guide step the chip says 'Showing you' and the step row says 'Showing you' (point_at). Errors read 'Problem  Something went wrong' above the real sentence. It makes the bubble look templated and wastes the header's limited width.
findings.evidence: Chromium render s-thinking.png and s-guiding.png. presenter.ts:591 and :692 (title 'Thinking…'), main.ts:864 and :889 (title 'Listening…'), TOOL_STEPS.point_at 'Showing you' (presenter.ts:252, 264) vs BUBBLE_LABEL.guiding 'Showing you' (bubble.ts:26), presenter.ts:529 and :780 ('Something went wrong').
findings.fix: Hide the title when it equals the chip's word (or drop the ellipsis title and let the chip carry it), vary the step text ('Pointing at it'), and title errors with what failed ('Couldn't reach Copilot') instead of 'Something went wrong'.

findings.title: Mixed first/third person and jargon in bubble copy
findings.scenario: One bubble says 'I can't reach Copilot' (title) and 'Ember can't reach GitHub right now. It will try again when the network is back.' (text). Others: 'Its running commands stop in 15 s unless the link comes back. Nothing new is sent meanwhile.' (static, 'link' and 's' jargon), 'Copying Ember's helper to build-01 (12 of 29 MB)…', 'Ember's Copilot runtime is missing or can't start. Reinstall Ember (sudo dnf reinstall ember).' and 'Ember connects with Windows' SSH. Add your key to Windows' ssh-agent, or connect once from PowerShell…'. The announcement 'On build-01. It starts in 4 seconds.' repeats the badge and stays '4 seconds' for the whole window. 'Thinking…' quotes the user's request cut at 120 characters with no ellipsis.
findings.evidence: host.ts:303-312 and :339 (titles vs explainStartError), runtime.ts:646 and :1085, remote tests pin 'Copying Ember's helper…'; presenter.ts:641-644 (announce text), :591 (slice(0, 120)).
findings.fix: Pick one voice (first person, as target-copy.ts's header says) and rewrite: 'build-01 hasn't answered for 5 seconds. Commands running there stop in 15 seconds unless it comes back.', 'Copying what Ember needs to build-01…', no commands in bubbles (settings only). Count the announcement down or say 'in a few seconds'. Add '…' when the quoted request is cut.

findings.title: target-copy.ts is a second, unused copy of the bubble words that unit tests pin
findings.scenario: ui-copy.test.ts pins sshSeen, offerConnect, connecting, connected, stalled, lost, commandQuestion, announcement and more from target-copy.ts, but the app imports only signInAgain from it. The real strings are inline in runtime.ts, flow.ts and presenter.ts and already differ: the pinned command question reads 'On build-01. It's shown in full in Ember's command window.' while flow.ts:671 sends 'On build-01: <first finding>' plus 'Your task: …'. Anyone editing the real wording gets no test failure, and the pinned copy gives false assurance.
findings.evidence: grep: only app/main/targets/runtime.ts:52 imports target-copy; test/unit/ui-copy.test.ts:565-599 asserts on its functions. Compare with runtime.ts:646, :692, :740 and flow.ts:671.
findings.fix: Have runtime/flow/presenter build their bubbles from these functions (then the tests pin what users see), or delete the unused functions and pin the real strings.

findings.title: A large answer opened with "Read all" can sit over Ember and the task cards
findings.scenario: With task cards stacked at the right and Ember beside them, the expanded answer (410×391 px) fits neither below, above nor beside Ember without covering the cards, so clearPlace falls back to a position that overlaps Ember's face. Cosmetic only (the bubble stays clickable), but it hides Ember while the user reads.
findings.evidence: Chromium sweep with two running tasks and an expanded answer: Ember at (1100,360) and (1250,360) gave the bubble at (712,8) and (862,8), size 410×391, overlapping Ember's body. Normal-size bubbles and long questions had no overlaps over a 42-position grid (cards, handle and Ember all cleared).
findings.fix: When no clear place exists for an expanded bubble, prefer a spot beside Ember over the cards' area, or shrink its max-height (16 lines) to fit the larger free side.

findings.title: After a dropped connection Ember silently switches to this computer and stays there after an automatic reconnect
findings.scenario: build-01 is the picked computer. The link drops and the bubble says 'Lost build-01 … I'll try to reconnect', without saying work moves to this computer, so the handle badge and ask-box chip just disappear. The reconnect then succeeds (adopt at line 1091). The bubble hides with no 'build-01 is back', and the picker stays on This computer. 'Check the disk' typed next runs here and its answer carries no 'on build-01' badge or note.
findings.evidence: onLinkState 'lost' calls setActive(LOCAL_TARGET) and shows the bubble text above. The progress 'ready' handler only runs adopt() and hideBubble(lost:…). test/unit/targets-runtime.test.ts line 700 asserts active 'local' after loss and nothing after the reconnect.
findings.fix: Say it in the lost bubble ('I'll work on this computer until it's back'). After an automatic reconnect show 'build-01 is back' with 'Work on build-01', or restore the picker if it was active when lost.

findings.title: Connection progress rewrites the bubble on every network chunk, over any answer or task the user is looking at
findings.scenario: While Ember downloads the 29 MB runtime or copies the helper, the user asks something else or a task is streaming. Each chunk replaces the visible bubble with 'Connecting to build-01… Downloading… (12 of 29 MB)'. The answer or task bubble flashes and is overwritten many times a second until the connect ends, and IPC to the overlay and handle is sent per chunk.
findings.evidence: Rig: 500 download progress events gave 500 showState bubble updates with only 30 distinct texts. The handler calls bubble() unconditionally and has no check on what the bubble currently shows.
findings.fix: Update only when the words or whole-MB figure changes, and only if no other bubble has replaced the connecting one since (shown.key). Otherwise show progress in the handle's status or the settings row.

findings.title: Connection failures, including 'host key changed', disappear after 14 s with no action; the documented 'identity changed' card is never shown and the bubble clips the fix
findings.scenario: For every non-retryable failure the bubble 'Can't connect to build-01' has no buttons and hides after 2*INFO_MS = 14 s. This applies to changed host key, too many keys, a config line SSH can't use, no OpenSSH, an old OpenSSH, no disk space, noexec/fapolicyd, the admin's allowedHosts and remote policy, and most of the messages in the docs' §4.8 table. They all carry a fix sentence. When the connect came from a 'Bring Ember' or Connect bubble, nothing else shows the reason (settings' message line only shows for connects started there). The changed-key text is 7 lines in a bubble whose error mood clips at 6, so 'then connect again.' is cut. The bubble is also dropped entirely while a Confirmer question is up (guardWhileAsking drops bubble patches and the runtime never re-shows it). docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §4.1 promises 'build-01's identity changed', but the 'host-key-changed' card (renderer/prompt/copy.ts:66, remote-ui.ts, prompt-window.ts) has no producer: promptCard() never creates it.
findings.evidence: Rig: failConnect(ConnectError kind host-key-changed, retry false) gave bubbles 'Connecting to build-01…' then 'Can't connect to build-01 | …Ember won't connect. If you know why… | actions [] | mood error', with one 14 s timer. Overlay render at 900x600: .eb-thought scrollHeight 140 vs clientHeight 120 for the key-changed text, overflow hidden, with a faded cut line. grep shows no code constructs kind 'host-key-changed' anywhere. guardWhileAsking (agent/confirm.ts:257) drops bubble patches while asking.
findings.fix: Show non-retryable failures until dismissed (a 'Close' button, plus 'Open settings' where it applies) and keep the last failure in the host's settings row. Produce the host-key-changed PromptCard (it is already built and validated) for that case instead of a bubble, or at least use the 'attention' mood (10 lines, scrollable). Re-show a runtime bubble that was dropped while a question was up.

findings.title: SSH, WSL and command-card bubble actions have no keyboard or screen-reader route, and the model is told to tell the user to 'click' them
findings.scenario: The overlay and handle windows are focusable:false, so bubble buttons cannot be tabbed to. Only Confirmer questions get global keys (Ctrl+Alt+Y/N, main.ts:655-662). Everything else is mouse-only: 'Bring Ember' / 'Not now' / 'Don't offer again' (SSH seen offer, runtime.ts:958-975), 'Connect' (offer_connect), Reconnect / Stop trying / Disconnect / Cancel, 'Read all' on a long answer, 'Show the command' / 'Read it' on a command or consent question, and Always in app (click-only by design). For offer_connect the tool result tells the model 'Tell them to click it' or 'connect it from Ember's menu' (runtime.ts:1382, 1389, 1189). The handle menu is not keyboard-reachable either. A keyboard or screen-reader user is told to click a button they cannot reach. Equivalent routes exist (Settings > Computers, Ctrl+Alt+X, Conversation in Settings) but are never mentioned.
findings.evidence: windows created with focusable:false (handle.ts:49, overlay.ts:282). bubbleAction ids owned by the targets runtime (runtime.ts:1420-1475) are plain bubble actions, not Confirmer questions, so Ctrl+Alt+Y/N does nothing for them (confirm.ts answerKey only reaches the current question). presenter.ts:769 'Read all' is ui:more. The live-region text built by announcement() (packages/bubble/src/bubble.ts:50-61) names no keys.
findings.fix: Say the keyboard route in the offer text and in the tool result ('or open Settings > Computers (Ctrl+Alt+E)'). Add key answers for offers (the same Ctrl+Alt+Y/N while an offer is up) or a focusable fallback, and give 'Read the last answer' a shortcut.

findings.title: Timeouts users cannot extend: questions expire after 120 s, answers and errors hide after 6-30 s with no way to pause
findings.scenario: A switch-access or one-handed user needs more than 2 minutes to reach Allow or Not now and the question silently expires as 'no'. A slow reader or a user with low vision gets an answer bubble that hides after 6000 ms plus 50 ms per character (30 s cap) and error notices after 12 s; the bubble is click-through, so hovering cannot hold it. INFO bubbles last 7 s (runtime.ts:391). The only retrieval routes are 'Read the last answer' in the mouse-only handle menu and the Conversation section in Settings.
findings.evidence: confirm.ts:97 `timeoutMs ?? 120_000`; presenter.ts:672 and :803 hideLater(min(30000, 6000 + n*50)); presenter.ts:532/546/783 12 000; main.ts:454 greeting 7 s or 15 s. No setting adjusts any of them; voice follow-up is a fixed 8 s too (README/consent text).
findings.fix: Add a 'Keep messages until I dismiss them' (or 'More time') setting that lengthens or disables the auto-hide and the question expiry, and give 'Read the last answer' a global shortcut.

findings.title: Question live-region text omits the answer keys; with Ember's speech disabled by policy a screen-reader user is never told them
findings.scenario: A question appears. The bubble shows its key hint ('Ctrl+Alt+Y allow · Ctrl+Alt+N not now') in the step row, but announcement() builds the live-region message from title and thought only. Ember's own spoken question adds 'Press Control Alt Y…' only when maySpeak() is true. If the organisation sets features.speak=false, the screen reader says 'Ember needs you: May I click Save…?' and never says how to answer, and the bubble's buttons are not reachable. For command questions the spoken text (questionWords) never names the keys or says to Alt+Tab to the command window.
findings.evidence: overlay.mjs live region: 'Ember needs you: May I click Save in Mousepad? Ember wants to click the Save button.' (step text appears in the page but not in the live region). main.ts:689-693 and runtime.ts:1566-1580 questionWords.
findings.fix: Append the step text (the key hint) to the announced message for mood 'attention' and, for command and consent questions, add 'It is in the Ember commands window; press Alt+Tab to read it'.

findings.title: Time units: "15 s" breaks across lines, and "s" mixes with "seconds"
findings.scenario: The stalled-connection bubble says "Its running commands stop in 15 s unless the link comes back." and in a 360 px card the line breaks between the number and its unit ("15" / "s unless…"). The announcement bubble says "in 4 seconds", the command window "Starts in 4 s.", and the status lines "3.2 s" and "2 min 5 s". "link" is jargon for the connection.
findings.evidence: Rendered the real handle card with that text (shots/handle-all.png, first panel): "Its running commands stop in 15 / s unless the link comes back." Sources: target-copy.ts:61, runtime.ts:646, command/copy.ts:35-43, 133 and 142.
findings.fix: Use "seconds" in sentences ("…stop in 15 seconds unless it answers again") and a no-break space (U+00A0) before the abbreviation in status lines ("3.2 s").

findings.title: One thing, several names: the organisation's model service, plus "machine" and "PC" among "computer"
findings.scenario: The organisation's own model endpoint is "model service" in Settings and the Setup check label, "AI endpoint" or "AI service" in bubble errors, "your organisation's endpoint" in the doctor detail and "AI service" in the README. Elsewhere the product says "this computer", but the settings tagline says "this machine" (and "a couple of things" even when one thing fails), and two consent lines say "another PC".
findings.evidence: presenter.ts:38, 40, 42, 47, 53 and 55; doctor.ts:165; home/main.ts:315 and 323; README.md:81; home/copy.ts:64; prompt/copy.ts:192 and remote-policy.ts:125 ("WSL on another PC"). The Setup check summary also says "to look at" while the CLI says "worth a look".
findings.fix: Pick "model service" everywhere. Change the tagline to "Ember needs N thing(s) fixed before it can work on this computer." and use "computer" in the two WSL lines.
